title: AI safety-evaluations ecosystem + the EA money map (AISIs, METR, Apollo, RSPs, DataRepublican)
source: Public record: US/UK AI Safety Institute (US renamed CAISI under the current admin), METR, Apollo Research, lab Responsible Scaling Policies / Preparedness frameworks; Open Philanthropy grant records; DataRepublican's 'EA Explorer' network map (datarepublican.com + Substack). Chronology overlay (structural; no financial-core edges). HONESTY: institutions, evals, RSPs, and grants = fact; 'safety-washing / regulatory-capture' critique = interpretation (labeled); DataRepublican's map is an INDEPENDENT open-source analysis with an explicitly critical POV - verbatim quotes link to sources, but funding-flow claims should be cross-checked against IRS 990s.

edges.notes: The US AI Safety Institute (housed at NIST; renamed the Center for AI Standards and Innovation / CAISI under the current administration) + the UK AISI run pre-deployment model testing - the government-eval layer of AI safety (fact; the rename + de-emphasis is itself a policy signal).
METR (Model Evaluation & Threat Research) runs dangerous-capability + autonomy evals (task-horizon benchmarks) that labs cite in safety cases; a central node in the eval ecosystem (fact).
Apollo Research specializes in deception / scheming evals - probing whether models strategically mislead; feeds lab + government safety assessments (fact).

Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP; AI Safety Levels) + OpenAI's Preparedness Framework are the labs' SELF-governance instruments - voluntary capability thresholds + commitments (fact of the frameworks; enforceability + sincerity graded).

Voluntary RSPs are pitched as the template for formal regulation - the mechanism by which lab self-governance becomes the policy baseline (critics call it regulatory capture / safety-washing; interpretation, labeled).

The evals + safety-org ecosystem (METR, Apollo, and many policy shops) is substantially EA-funded - Open Philanthropy (+ SFF/FLI) grants - so the same EA money funds the labs, the evaluators, AND the policy advocates (fact of funding; conflict-of-interest framing interpretation).

The EA movement is the throughline connecting frontier-lab safety teams, the eval nonprofits, and the pause/pacing policy push (SB 1047, the 2026 pacing letters -> Buist) - the network a 'follow the money' trace keeps landing on (fact of the linkages; coordinated-intent claims remain unsupported, per spec-buist-v-anthropic-pacing).

DataRepublican (pseudonymous open-source data analyst; site tagline 'Exposing where the money flows') published 'EA Explorer' (Sep 2026) - a people-and-funding NETWORK MAP + a verbatim-quote browser over 25+GB of EA forum material, motivated by the follow-the-money scrutiny after Jacob Coxon's viral Anthropic-resignation/pause post + the tracing to METR/EA. INDEPENDENT analysis with an explicitly critical POV: quotes link to sources, but funding claims should be cross-checked vs IRS 990s (fact of the tool; her framing = her viewpoint, labeled). https://datarepublican.com/

Her charity-graph tooling (multi-root BFS over 990 filings, taxpayer-fund tracing) is applied to the EA/Open-Philanthropy grant network - the same funding rails this map tracks, from an independent methodology (fact of the tool + method; specific dollar attributions = verify vs 990s).
